rules.title: Santa Ana just cause eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Once you have lived in your unit for 30 days, your landlord can end your tenancy only for a listed just cause, stated in a written notice. For at-fault causes you must first get a chance to fix the problem. For no-fault evictions the landlord must pay 3 months of relocation assistance or waive your last 3 months of rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 30 days of occupancy; 3 months relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault evictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in Santa Ana after 30 days of occupancy, except housing produced in the last 15 years.
rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; other shared living quarters.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (Santa Ana Mun. Code)

exemption_tests.description: Housing produced in the last 15 years is exempt.

rules.reason: Two official city pages describe the just-cause provisions of the same Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance, so I merged them. The detailed D085 text supplies the quote, the date and the exemptions.
